sources.title: Age-Structured Survival and Reproduction
sources.publisher: Mississippi State University Deer Ecology and Management Lab
sources.scope: White-tailed deer; age, density and habitat concepts with Mississippi examples
sources.use: Structural rationale for age-dependent survival and reproduction
sources.limitation: Not a complete age-by-sex life table; no lifespan or numeric survival profile extracted

sources.title: The difference between killing and eating: ecological shortcomings of puma energetic models
sources.scope: Primary field study in California, Colorado and Patagonia
sources.use: Separate kills, consumption, carcass access and loss; energy alone is insufficient to predict kills
sources.limitation: Do not translate pooled biomass estimates into a universal daily food requirement or attack probability

sources.title: Lions in the Santa Monica Mountains
sources.scope: Santa Monica Mountains study area, California; facts section dated December 19, 2022
sources.evidenceType: Agency account of its field monitoring
sources.use: Check spatial scale and site-specific predator-prey plausibility
sources.limitation: Descriptive local observations, not probability distributions; not production constants or a claim about current abundance

sources.title: Wildlife-Vehicle Collision Reduction Study: Report to Congress, Chapter 2
sources.scope: US collision literature and historical collision data
sources.evidenceType: Commissioned technical report with analyses and literature review
sources.use: Require exposure, time, traffic, species and landscape context; distinguish data denominators
sources.limitation: Archived report, not current local per-deer collision rates; does not validate the prototype Poisson model

calibrationRequirements: Select region and scientific species identities before applying field rates
Age-sex survival curves with study interval, sample size, uncertainty and censoring method
Cause-specific mortality compatible with survival, without double-counting explicit events
Species reproduction, juvenile survival, maturation and seasonal timing
Predator food/energy budgets separately from kill rates and prey selection
Movement, territory, outside-ranch exposure and road-crossing behavior
Fish growth, spawning, water quality, temperature and size-selective predation
Bird nesting, fledging, migration and supporting prey/vegetation
Independent validation observations and sensitivity analyses across seeds
runtimeParameterPolicy: All current test parameters are synthetic. No reviewed source has been promoted to a calibrated production probability.
